target_customer: Frequent travelers and business travelers buying premium connected carry-on luggage (consumers)
problem: Lost, delayed or stolen luggage and hassle with weighing, locking and charging devices while traveling.
business_model: Hardware sales of smart luggage, crowdfunded first, then direct and retail sales

founders.name: Diego Saez-Gil
previous_startups: WeHostels (hostel booking, later sold to StudentUniverse)

founders.name: Tomi Pierucci
founders.background_notes: TechCrunch 2015-01-23 cites hardware experience; school not named.

founders.name: Alejo Verlini
founders.background_notes: The only founder listed on the YC page.

exit.reason: Company announced shutdown on 2018-05-01 after US airlines banned smart luggage with non-removable batteries; Travelpro acquired technology, designs, brand and IP.

competitors.name: Airbus Bag2Go
competitors.what: Similar connected luggage concept announced earlier

competitors.name: Samsonite and Tumi
competitors.what: Incumbent premium luggage brands used as positioning benchmarks, not smart luggage rivals

technical_complexity.rationale: Hardware with GPS, scale, lock, charger and app, battery safety and manufacturing; hard for a small team and later hit by airline battery rules.

defensibility.rationale: Patents existed per patent analytics sites, but luggage incumbents and later entrants (Away, Raden, Samsonite) could add features; no network effects.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Samsonite and others later launched tracking luggage lines. The decisive blow came from airline policy in 2018, and Travelpro bought the assets.

market_need_then: Indiegogo campaign in October 2014 hit its goal in two hours and pre-sold 10,000 units to 114 countries, collecting about $2.2M.

identity.visual_style: Premium design; Red Dot Best of the Best award for the carry-on
identity.voice_and_tone: Aspirational travel tech; CEO compared the brand ambition to Tumi, Samsonite and GoPro (TechCrunch 2015)

branding.brand_signature: The world's first smart connected carry-on
branding.community_and_virality: More than 10,000 Indiegogo backers across 120 countries, and a second Indiegogo campaign for Series 2 that raised about $1M in 2017 (Crowdfund Insider).

brand_strength.rationale: Viral crowdfunding, design awards (Red Dot Best of the Best, Forbes and Fast Company recognition per YC page) and wide review coverage made it the best known smart luggage brand of its time.

outcome_analysis: Bluesmart pre-sold more than 10,000 smart carry-ons through Indiegogo in 2014 and raised venture and strategic money in 2015 and 2017, but its original bag had a non-removable battery. When major US airlines banned such luggage in early 2018, the company said it was in an irreversibly difficult financial and business situation, shut down on May 1, 2018 and sold its technology, designs and brand to Travelpro. The directory lists it as acquired, but in substance it was a shutdown with an asset sale.
notes: Exit type is acquisition to match the directory status, but the facts are a shutdown plus asset sale to Travelpro. Funding sources conflict: Skift describes 2015 as $6.5M notes and $5M venture debt plus $5.5M new money, with the notes converted to a Series A, while Endeavor reports a $12M Series A in January 2017; the 2015 and 2017 entries may overlap. The $11.5M and $12M pages were identified from search results and not opened (Phocuswire returned 403). The site bluesmart.com is a frameset with no readable content. Founder education beyond Pierucci's PhD not found. No named dated Samsonite smart product competitor in 2015.
